misconceptions.description: Calm, documented answers to questions people often ask: the Kaaba, how Islam spread, and the wisdom behind some rulings.

id-name.question: Do I have to change my name to be a true Muslim?
id-name.principle: No. Changing your name is not a condition for your Islam to be valid; a person enters Islam through the two testimonies of faith and belief in their meaning, not through a name. Many of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) kept the names they were known by before Islam. The Prophet ﷺ changed only particular names whose meanings were inappropriate — for example, he changed the name ʿĀṣiyah (“disobedient”) to Jamīlah (“beautiful”). What matters is the meaning of the name: if it is good or neutral, there is no harm in keeping it.
id-name.culture: Choosing a new Arabic name is a widespread custom among new Muslims. It is permissible for anyone who wishes to, but it is not a religious condition or a sign of sincere Islam. Many names used in Muslim countries are themselves local, non-Arabic names.
guidance: Check the meaning of your current name; if it is good or ordinary, keep it without hesitation.
If your name carries a meaning that contradicts belief — such as declaring servitude to other than Allah — it should be changed.
If you would like a new name, you may choose one; pick a name with a good meaning.
Changing your name on official documents is an optional administrative step that follows the laws of your country.

id-father-name.question: Should I change my father's name or my family name after becoming Muslim?
id-father-name.principle: Your lineage stays attributed to your real father, even if he is not Muslim; Islam commands that children be called after their fathers and protects lineage. So someone who becomes Muslim should not replace their father's name with another name as if it were their father. As for writing “son/daughter of Abdullah” instead of the father's name, scholars have discussed it, so ask a fatwa body before doing so.
id-father-name.culture: Some new Muslims think a non-Muslim father's name must be replaced. This is a common misunderstanding with no basis: your father's name is part of your lineage and your family identity.
guidance: Keep your father's name and your family name in your lineage as they are.
There is no harm in a kunya (such as Abu … or Umm …) or a name people know you by, as long as you do not attribute yourself to anyone other than your father.
If your official documents are going to be changed, ask the fatwa body in your country before changing your father's name.

id-arabic.question: Do I have to learn Arabic for my Islam to be valid?
id-arabic.principle: Knowing Arabic is not a condition for your Islam to be valid. Allah made the diversity of languages one of His signs, and Islam is a religion for all people. Entering Islam only requires saying the two testimonies of faith while understanding their meaning. However, the prayer has recitations and words of remembrance said in Arabic, so a Muslim learns what they need of them for their worship — such as Sūrat al-Fātiḥah — gradually and according to their ability; Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
id-arabic.culture: Mastering Arabic is a virtue that helps in understanding the Quran and Sunnah, but the feeling that a “real” Muslim is an Arab or an Arabic speaker is a cultural perception, not a correct one; most Muslims in the world today are not Arabs.
guidance: Start by learning the meaning of the two testimonies of faith, then Sūrat al-Fātiḥah and the basic words of the prayer.
Use an approved translation of the meanings of the Quran in your language to understand what you read.
Learn Arabic gradually if you can, without letting that delay your worship now.

id-clothes.question: Do I have to wear Arab clothes, or the clothes of a particular country, to be a Muslim?
id-clothes.principle: Islam does not impose a particular national dress. It sets general guidelines for clothing: covering the ʿawrah (the parts of the body that must be covered), modesty, and avoiding what the Sharia prohibits. Any clothing that meets these guidelines is permissible, whether it comes from your own people or from elsewhere. The Quran describes the garment of taqwā (God-consciousness) as the best.
id-clothes.culture: The thobe, the shemagh and similar garments are the traditional clothing of some peoples, not obligatory religious dress. Wearing them is not a sign of greater religiosity, and not wearing them does not lessen it.
guidance: Wear modest clothing that covers what must be covered, suited to your society.
Men and women have specific rulings on clothing; learn them from a reliable source.
Women have rulings on hijab; see the hijab question in the “Daily life” category.

fam-visit.question: Can I visit my non-Muslim family and be kind to them?
fam-visit.principle: Yes. Islam commands honouring parents, keeping ties with relatives and being kind to them even if they are not Muslim, as long as they are not at war with Muslims. The Prophet ﷺ allowed Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr (may Allah be pleased with them) to keep ties with her mother while she was a polytheist, and the Quran commands keeping company with one's parents in this world with kindness even if they urge their child to associate partners with Allah — while not obeying them in that. Islam does not cut family ties; it adds more kindness to them.
fam-visit.culture: Some new Muslims think they must distance themselves from their families or cut them off, and they may hear this from some people. This is not part of the religion; good character with your family is one of the best ways to introduce them to Islam.
guidance: Visit your family, keep in touch and be kind to them with gifts and kind words.
Do not obey them in anything that goes against your religion, and explain this gently and respectfully.
If a specific situation, such as a religious occasion, puts you in an awkward position, see the question on holidays in this category.
Be a role model through your character; it speaks louder than arguments.

fam-tell.question: How do I tell my family that I became Muslim?
fam-tell.principle: The basis for dealing with your family and inviting them is wisdom and good counsel, making things easy and not driving people away. So choose the right time and the right way, and present Islam as it truly is through your character and your respect for them, while holding firmly to your religion.
fam-tell.culture: There is no religious formula or ceremony required to announce your Islam to your family; how and when you tell them depends on your circumstances and your family's culture.
guidance: Start with the person who is closest to you and most understanding.
Explain what drew you to Islam, and assure them that your love and respect for them will not change.
Avoid heated arguments, and give them time to accept the news.
If you fear harm to yourself, consult a trusted Sharia specialist in your country before telling them.

fam-holidays.question: Should I take part in my family's religious holidays?
fam-holidays.khilafAgreed: Scholars agree that a Muslim does not take part in the religious rites and rituals of other faiths, while the duty of kindness towards family and keeping ties with them remains.
fam-holidays.khilafNote: As for the details connected to these holidays — such as greetings, attending a family gathering held on the day of the holiday without taking part in its rites, or exchanging gifts — contemporary scholars hold different views and distinctions, and I do not choose between them.
guidance: Keep your ties with your family on other days too; kindness is not tied to an occasion.
Avoid taking part in the rituals and rites themselves.
For details specific to your situation, ask a trusted Sharia specialist in your country.
Explain your position to your family gently and respectfully.

fam-marriage.question: I became Muslim and my husband (or wife) is not Muslim. What is the ruling on our marriage?
fam-marriage.principle: Islam has detailed rulings for someone who becomes Muslim while their spouse does not, and jurists have explained them according to different circumstances; that is why the case must be presented, with its details, to people of knowledge.
fam-marriage.referReason: This is a personal case concerning an existing marriage contract, and the ruling depends on many details — for example, which spouse became Muslim, the religion of the other spouse, whether the waiting period (ʿiddah) has passed, whether there are children, and the laws in your country. So Basirah does not give a ruling on it.
fam-marriage.referTo: A qualified mufti or an official fatwa body in your country, or a Sharia specialist at a recognised Islamic centre that cares for new Muslims.
guidance: Do not make a hasty decision about your marriage before asking people of knowledge.
Write down the full details of your situation (when you became Muslim, your spouse's religion, whether you have children) before contacting the mufti.
Be gentle and treat your family well during this period.

wor-gradual.question: I can't apply everything at once — is my Islam still accepted?
wor-gradual.principle: A person enters Islam through the two testimonies of faith and then learns its rulings step by step, and Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity. So begin with what matters most — and the most important duty after the testimonies of faith is the prayer. Learning gradually does not mean leaving what you know to be obligatory and are able to do; rather, do your best in what you can and keep learning.
wor-gradual.culture: Some new Muslims are loaded from day one with a great deal of detail and customs by the people around them, and think their Islam is not valid unless they master all of it. Much of what is asked of them is custom, recommended acts, or details that can be learned later.
guidance: Focus now on understanding tawhid and on learning and performing the prayer.
Learn something new every week, even if it is small, and keep it up.
Do not compare yourself with people who grew up Muslim; everyone has their own journey.
Look for a teacher at a nearby mosque or Islamic centre to accompany you as you learn.

wor-ghusl.question: Do I have to take a ritual bath (ghusl) when I enter Islam?
wor-ghusl.khilafAgreed: Taking a ghusl upon entering Islam is part of the Sharia; it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ instructed some people who embraced Islam to do so.
wor-ghusl.khilafNote: Scholars differ on its ruling: whether it is obligatory for everyone who embraces Islam or recommended, with some scholars making distinctions in particular situations. This is a matter of scholarly reasoning (ijtihad), and I do not choose between the views.
guidance: Learn the correct way to perform ghusl; you will need it in your worship.
To know the view followed by the scholars you rely on, ask a Sharia specialist.

wor-prayer-start.question: How do I start learning the prayer when I don't know any Quran by heart?
wor-prayer-start.principle: The prayer is the greatest deed after the testimonies of faith, and the Prophet ﷺ instructed us to pray as we saw him pray; so the prayer is learned by watching and practising. The most important thing to start memorising is Sūrat al-Fātiḥah, because it is recited in every unit (rakʿah) of the prayer, then the basic words of remembrance. Scholars have explained what someone who has not yet memorised should do until they do; Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity, so do not delay the prayer because you have not memorised yet.
wor-prayer-start.culture: Some postures in the prayer differ slightly between worshippers according to the recognised schools of jurisprudence (madhhabs), so do not worry if you see small differences between people; this reflects the breadth of fiqh and is not necessarily a mistake.
guidance: Ask your mosque imam or an Islamic centre to teach you the prayer in practice.
Start memorising al-Fātiḥah section by section while understanding its meaning.
Learn wudu (ablution) before the prayer; it is a condition for the prayer to be valid.
Pray in congregation at the mosque whenever you can; it is one of the fastest ways to learn.

bel-tawhid.question: What does tawhid mean?
bel-tawhid.principle: Simply put: to believe that Allah alone created this universe and runs it, that He alone deserves to be worshipped so nothing is worshipped alongside Him, and that He is described by the beautiful names and lofty attributes He has described Himself with, without likening Him to His creation. This is what Muslims call “tawhid”; it is the meaning of the testimony “There is no god but Allah”, and it is the purpose for which people were created.
bel-tawhid.culture: Translating “tawhid” only as “Oneness of God” can suggest mere numerical oneness. It is more accurate to keep the term Tawhid and explain its meaning: singling out Allah in His lordship, in worship, and in His names and attributes.
guidance: Reflect on the meaning of “There is no god but Allah”: nothing deserves worship except Allah.
Read Sūrat al-Ikhlāṣ and reflect on its meaning; it summarises tawhid.
Direct your supplication and your worship to Allah alone.

bel-quran.question: Was the Quran written by Muhammad ﷺ?
bel-quran.principle: Muslims believe that the Quran is the speech of Allah the Exalted, revealed to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the angel Jibrīl (Gabriel), peace be upon him, and not authored by him. Among the evidence the Quran itself mentions: the Prophet ﷺ did not read or write before it was revealed; the Quran challenged the most eloquent people to produce a single chapter like it, and they did not; and although it was revealed over many years, it contains no inconsistency or contradiction. Muslims also clearly distinguish between the Quran and the Prophet's own words transmitted in hadith.
guidance: Read an approved translation of the meanings of the Quran in your language, and reflect on its style and content yourself.
Notice the difference between the style of the Quran and the style of the Prophet's hadith.
For detailed questions, see the approved question-and-answer sources on the “References” page.

bel-past-sins.question: Are the sins I committed before Islam forgiven?
bel-past-sins.principle: Yes. Islam wipes out the sins that came before it, as the Prophet ﷺ told ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with him) when he embraced Islam. Allah has promised that those who desist from disbelief will be forgiven what has passed, and He even replaces the bad deeds of those who repent with good deeds. So begin your new page with peace of mind, and do not despair of Allah's mercy.
bel-past-sins.culture: Many new Muslims feel the weight of their past, and some people may say things that add to their anxiety. The basis in Islam is good news and opening the door of hope.
guidance: Turn to acts of obedience with a calm heart, and do not dwell on what has passed.
If you owe other people rights, such as debts or things entrusted to you, ask people of knowledge how to fulfil them.
Seek forgiveness often and do good deeds; both bring more peace to the heart.

bel-enter.question: What do I need to do to enter Islam? Do I need witnesses or an official certificate?
bel-enter.principle: A person enters Islam by saying the two testimonies of faith while believing in their meaning: “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.” The two testimonies are the first of the five pillars of Islam, followed by prayer, zakat, fasting and Hajj. Witnesses, an imam or a document are not conditions for Islam to be valid.
bel-enter.culture: The certificate of embracing Islam issued by some bodies is a useful administrative document for official purposes, such as marriage or travelling for Hajj, but it is not a condition for Islam to be valid.
guidance: Say the two testimonies of faith while believing in their meaning.
Learn the meaning of the two testimonies and the five pillars of Islam.
If you need an official document, contact an Islamic centre or the competent authority in your country.

day-work.question: My job involves things that go against the Sharia. Do I have to leave it?
day-work.principle: The basic principle is that a Muslim seeks lawful earnings and is mindful of Allah as much as they are able; whoever is mindful of Allah, He will make a way out for them and provide for them from where they do not expect.
day-work.referReason: Judging a particular job depends precisely on its nature, the kind of violation involved, your role in it, your living circumstances and the alternatives available to you. This is a personal fatwa, which Basirah does not issue.
day-work.referTo: A qualified mufti or an official fatwa body, explaining the full details of your work.
guidance: Do not rush to leave your job before asking people of knowledge about your case in detail.
Write an accurate description of your tasks and of what you see as problematic in them.
At the same time, look for alternatives and other job opportunities.
Seek help through supplication and patience.

day-hijab.question: Is hijab obligatory? And is covering the face obligatory?
day-hijab.khilafAgreed: Scholars agree that hijab is obligatory for an adult Muslim woman, meaning she covers her body and hair in front of men who are not her mahram; the evidence for this is in the Quran.
day-hijab.khilafNote: They differ on the ruling of covering the face and hands: some consider it obligatory and others recommended, and each view has its evidence. This is a matter of ijtihad, and I do not choose between the views. As for your own circumstances in applying hijab, such as your workplace or family, present them to a trusted scholar.
guidance: Learn the conditions of the Islamic hijab from a reliable source.
If you face particular difficulties in your environment, consult a female Sharia specialist who knows your circumstances.
Remember that hijab is an act of worship for Allah, and wearing it with good character is one of the most beautiful forms of daʿwah.

day-circumcision.question: Is circumcision obligatory for someone who embraces Islam as an adult?
day-circumcision.khilafAgreed: Circumcision is one of the practices of the fitrah (natural disposition) mentioned by the Prophet ﷺ, and the validity of one's Islam does not depend on it.
day-circumcision.khilafNote: Scholars differ on its ruling for men — whether it is obligatory or a confirmed sunnah — and also on its ruling for someone who embraces Islam as an adult and fears harm. Because the matter is one of ijtihad and relates to a personal health situation, I do not choose between the views.
guidance: Do not worry: your Islam is valid and does not depend on circumcision.
Ask a trusted scholar about its ruling in your case.
Consult a specialist doctor about the health aspect before any decision.

und-differ.question: Why are there different rulings among scholars?
und-differ.principle: The rulings of Islam are of two kinds: definitive ones, established by clear texts and agreed upon by scholars — such as the obligation of the prayer and the prohibition of alcohol; and matters of ijtihad, where a text can be understood in more than one way or there is no explicit text, so qualified scholars reason about the evidence and reach different views. This recognised difference is not a contradiction, and the Prophet ﷺ approved it: when the Companions understood his instruction to pray ʿAṣr at Banū Qurayẓah in different ways, he did not rebuke any of them, and he said that a judge who strives and is right has two rewards, and one who strives and errs has one reward.
und-differ.culture: The number of schools and opinions can seem confusing to a new Muslim. The well-known schools of jurisprudence (Ḥanafī, Mālikī, Shāfiʿī and Ḥanbalī) are scholarly schools for understanding the evidence, not different religions or rival sects.
guidance: Distinguish between matters that are agreed upon and matters of ijtihad.
In matters of ijtihad, follow a trusted scholar whose knowledge and religion you are confident in.
Respect those who hold a different recognised view in a matter of ijtihad; this is part of the etiquette of disagreement.

und-all-agree.question: Do all Muslims agree on every issue?
und-all-agree.principle: No. Muslims agree on the foundations and definitive matters of the religion — such as belief in Allah alone, the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, the pillars of Islam and of faith, and the prohibition of clearly forbidden things. But on many secondary issues there is recognised difference among scholars. So it is not correct to attribute agreement to Muslims on an issue unless it is established, nor to portray every difference as an attack on the foundation of the religion.
und-all-agree.culture: A new Muslim may see different customs among Muslims from different countries and think this is a difference in religion, while much of it is social custom or recognised juristic difference.
guidance: When you hear “Muslims unanimously agree”, check the source.
Ask yourself: is this issue one of the foundations, or a matter of ijtihad?
Rely on the trusted sources listed on the “References” page.

und-fatwa.question: What is the difference between general information and a fatwa? When should I ask a mufti?
und-fatwa.principle: General information explains a ruling or concept as it is in the sources, such as the obligation of the prayer or the meaning of tawhid. A fatwa is a religious answer given by a qualified scholar about a particular situation or question after knowing its details, because the ruling can differ with circumstances. That is why Basirah gives documented general information and refers you to people of knowledge for personal cases.
guidance: Use Basirah to understand the foundations and general information.
If your question is about your own situation (marriage, divorce, inheritance, work, a financial transaction), ask a mufti.
Choose an official fatwa body or a scholar known for knowledge and trustworthiness.

mis-kaaba.question: Why do Muslims face the Kaaba? Do they worship it?
mis-kaaba.principle: Muslims do not worship the Kaaba; they worship Allah alone. The Kaaba is the qiblah — the direction Allah commanded Muslims to face in their prayer — so their direction is united all over the world. The Quran commands worshipping the Lord of this House, not the House itself, and makes clear that righteousness is not merely turning towards a direction. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) said to the Black Stone that it is a stone that can neither harm nor benefit, and that he kissed it only to follow the Prophet ﷺ.
guidance: Remember that the qiblah is a direction for prayer, and the One worshipped is Allah alone.
If someone asks you about it, explain calmly: the qiblah unites Muslims, and worship is for Allah.
You can find the direction of the qiblah with a trusted app or by asking at a nearby mosque.

mis-sword.question: Did Islam spread by the sword?
mis-sword.principle: The established rule in the Quran is that there is no compulsion in religion; faith is not valid under compulsion because it rests on the conviction of the heart. The wars Muslims fought in history have Islamic rulings and limits — including the prohibition of aggression — and their own political and historical context, and they did not mean forcing individuals to change their religion. This is supported by the fact that non-Muslims lived for centuries under Muslim states keeping their religions, and that Islam spread across vast regions, such as South-East Asia, through traders and callers to Islam.
mis-sword.culture: It is important to distinguish between the teachings of Islam itself and the actions of states and individuals throughout history; history contains right and wrong, and it is judged by the standard of the Sharia, not the other way round. Projecting one picture onto a history that spans centuries and continents does not give an accurate understanding.
guidance: Distinguish between the historical question about wars and Islam's ruling on compulsion in religion.
Read about how Islam spread in South-East Asia and Africa through trade and daʿwah.
For more, refer to the approved sources on the Prophet's biography and history on the “References” page.

mis-alcohol.question: Why does Islam forbid alcohol? Isn't that a restriction on freedom?
mis-alcohol.principle: The prohibition of alcohol is established by the Quran and the Sunnah and is an agreed-upon matter. The wisdom the Quran explains is that its sin and harm are greater than its benefit, and one of the major objectives of the Sharia is protecting the mind, because the mind is the basis of responsibility and through it a person protects themselves, their family and their society. The prohibition here protects the person rather than restricting them; freedom in Islam is a responsible freedom that does not include what harms oneself and others.
mis-alcohol.culture: In some cultures drinking alcohol is part of social occasions, and a new Muslim may feel awkward about this. Declining politely, with good character, preserves your relationships without compromising your religion.
guidance: Avoid every intoxicant, whether a little or a lot.
Excuse yourself politely at social occasions, and suggest an alternative.
If you find it hard to stop, seek support from a specialist and from Muslims who can help you.

h_asma.narrator: Asmāʾ bint Abī Bakr (may Allah be pleased with them both) said:
h_asma.text: My mother came to me while she was a polytheist, in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “My mother has come and she wishes (to be close to me) — shall I keep ties with my mother?” He said: “Yes, keep ties with your mother.”

h_hadm.narrator: From the hadith of ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with him) when he embraced Islam, the Prophet ﷺ said to him:
h_hadm.text: “Do you not know that Islam wipes out what came before it?”

h_khams.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
h_khams.text: “Islam is built upon five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establishing the prayer, giving zakat, Hajj, and fasting Ramadan.”

h_haqq.narrator: From the hadith of Muʿādh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him), the Prophet ﷺ said:
h_haqq.text: “The right of Allah over His servants is that they worship Him and associate nothing with Him.”

h_asia.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) reported:
h_asia.text: That a daughter of ʿUmar was called ʿĀṣiyah (“disobedient”), so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ named her Jamīlah (“beautiful”).

h_yassiru.narrator: Anas ibn Mālik (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
h_yassiru.text: “Make things easy and do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.”

h_muadh.narrator: Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) reported that the Prophet ﷺ sent Muʿādh to Yemen and said:
h_muadh.text: “Call them to testify that there is no god but Allah and that I am the Messenger of Allah. If they accept that, then teach them that Allah has made five prayers obligatory upon them in every day and night.”

h_adwamuha.narrator: ʿĀʾishah (may Allah be pleased with her) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
h_adwamuha.text: “The deeds most beloved to Allah the Exalted are those done most consistently, even if they are few.”
h_adwamuha.source: Sahih al-Bukhari (6464) and Sahih Muslim (783); the wording is Muslim's

h_salli.narrator: Mālik ibn al-Ḥuwayrith (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
h_salli.text: “Pray as you have seen me praying.”

h_qays.narrator: Qays ibn ʿĀṣim (may Allah be pleased with him) reported:
h_qays.text: That he embraced Islam, and the Prophet ﷺ told him to wash (take a ghusl) with water and lote-tree leaves (sidr).
h_qays.source: Jamiʿ al-Tirmidhi (605), whose wording this is; Sunan Abi Dawud (355); Sunan al-Nasaʾi (188)
h_qays.grade: Graded hasan by al-Tirmidhi and sahih by al-Albani

h_ijtihad.narrator: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ (may Allah be pleased with him) heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say:
h_ijtihad.text: “When a judge gives a ruling, strives (in ijtihad) and is right, he has two rewards; and when he gives a ruling, strives and errs, he has one reward.”

h_qurayza.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) reported that on the day of al-Aḥzāb the Prophet ﷺ said:
h_qurayza.text: “No one should pray ʿAṣr except at Banū Qurayẓah.” The time of ʿAṣr came upon some of them on the way. Some said: “We will not pray until we reach it”, and others said: “Rather, we will pray; that is not what was meant by us.” This was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he did not rebuke any of them.

h_halal.narrator: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr (may Allah be pleased with them both) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
h_halal.text: “What is lawful is clear and what is unlawful is clear, and between them are doubtful matters that many people do not know.”

h_umar_stone.narrator: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) came to the Black Stone, kissed it and said:
h_umar_stone.text: “I know that you are a stone that can neither harm nor benefit. Had I not seen the Prophet ﷺ kissing you, I would not have kissed you.”

h_fitra.narrator: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
h_fitra.text: “Five things are part of the fitrah: circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, trimming the moustache, clipping the nails and plucking the armpit hair.”

h_kadhib.narrator: Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:
h_kadhib.text: “Whoever lies about me deliberately, let him take his seat in the Fire.”
h_kadhib.source: Sahih al-Bukhari (110) and the introduction to Sahih Muslim (3)

h_muskir.narrator: Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:
h_muskir.text: “Every intoxicant is khamr, and every intoxicant is unlawful.”

glossary.الإسلام: The religion of submitting to Allah through tawhid and yielding to Him in obedience. Explain it according to context; do not reduce it to a general cultural meaning.
glossary.التوحيد: Preferably keep the term and explain its meaning: singling out Allah in lordship and worship, and describing Him with the names given in revelation. Do not reduce it to a translation that may suggest mere numerical oneness.
glossary.العبادة: Includes the actions of the heart, speech and deeds by which a servant draws near to Allah; it is not limited to rituals.
glossary.النبوة: Used for Allah's choosing of prophets to receive revelation, distinguished from human religious leadership.
glossary.الوحي: Explained as what Allah revealed to His prophets, avoiding loose uses that could suggest personal inspiration.
glossary.الشريعة: Explained according to context; not reduced to punishments or criminal law.
glossary.الحديث: What is transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ of his sayings, actions or approvals and the like, stating its degree of authenticity when used as evidence.
glossary.السنة: The guidance and way of the Prophet ﷺ; the intended meaning is determined by the scholarly context.
glossary.الفتوى: A religious answer given by a qualified person about a situation or question; not to be equated with general information.
glossary.الدعوة: Introducing Islam and inviting to it with wisdom; the English equivalent is chosen according to context and audience.

A.title: Settled original information
A.scope: The Quran, authentic approved hadith, the pillars of Islam and of faith, the basic biography of the Prophet ﷺ, morals and values, settled introductory information.
A.handling: A direct answer documented with its source.

B.title: Explanation, definition and reasoning
B.scope: Explaining concepts, comparisons, the objectives of the Sharia, answering intellectual questions and general doubts.
B.handling: Answer from the approved material showing the reference, and avoid categorical statements where difference is possible.

C.title: Disputed or highly sensitive matters
C.scope: Juristic difference, detailed creedal issues, controversial historical issues, questions that need special scholarly treatment.
C.handling: An answer limited to what is approved, or stating that there is a difference, or referral to a specialist.

D.title: Fatwa or personal case
D.scope: A ruling on an individual situation, the validity of a specific person's contract or worship, a family dispute, legal or medical matters with a religious effect.
D.handling: The system gives no independent ruling; it explains general information and refers to a qualified body.

sources.content: The Digital Daʿwah Repository and the al-Jamhara encyclopedia of Islamic-content terms. Recommended for the topics and terms needed in daʿwah, and for daʿwah by country, by religion, by language and by audience.
The Quranic text in the approved script and text, with approved translations for each language used (the King Fahd Complex edition or its translations, or those on Quranpedia).
sources.rule: Make sure verses are transmitted reliably.

sources.content: Any Islamic sources from the first three centuries, or the Dorar.net tafsir platform.
sources.rule: Used to explain a verse, distinguishing the exegete's words from the Quranic text.

sources.content: Authentic hadith from the two Sahihs, and what is added from other books of Sunnah after confirming its authenticity if it is to be relied on (refer to the Dorar.net hadith encyclopedia, or the approved editions of the books of Sunnah on al-Maktaba al-Shamela).
sources.rule: No hadith is attributed without a source and an approved grading in the data.

sources.content: Any Islamic sources from the first three centuries, or the Dorar.net creed platform.
sources.rule: Adhere to what Muslims are upon, especially the Companions, the Successors and those who followed them.

sources.content: Any approved book of fiqh in one of the four schools, or the Dorar.net fiqh encyclopedia.
sources.rule: Must not turn into a personal fatwa or an independent automated preference (tarjīḥ).

sources.content: Any Islamic sources from the first three centuries, or the Dorar.net history platform.
sources.rule: Rely on established events, and indicate what needs caution.

sources.content: Bayyināt: questions and answers about Islam.
sources.rule: A primary source for conversational solutions dealing with doubts.
Takes precedence over automatic translation for sensitive Islamic terms.

standards.title: Reliability and attribution
standards.text: Every religious fact, quotation or ruling the solution presents must be traceable to its source; no text or statement may be attributed to a reference that does not contain it; religious text must be distinguished from generated explanation; and insufficient information must be stated when needed.
standards.applied: The text of every verse is taken from the King Fahd Complex Mushaf, and a verse is shown only if the model read its tafsir while answering; hadith come from a closed, verified registry; each piece of evidence appears in its own card with its source and a verification link, and any quotation that does not match the text is removed automatically before display.

standards.title: Distinguishing the definitive from the disputed
standards.text: Disputed matters and matters of ijtihad are not presented categorically, and the difference is indicated as far as the context needs, without overwhelming the user with detail that does not serve their purpose.
standards.applied: A separate “Scholarly difference” card states what is agreed upon, declares that there is a difference, and does not choose between the views.

standards.title: No independent fatwas
standards.text: The system does not independently issue personal fatwas or rule on matters that require knowing the facts or specialised religious judgement; it uses referral or asks for clarification when needed.
standards.applied: Automatic detection of personal cases (level D) before and after the model, turning them into a “Needs a specialist” card showing where to go.

standards.title: Resisting hallucination
standards.text: When there is no sufficient reference or confidence is low, the priority is to abstain, be cautious or refer — not to generate an undocumented answer.
standards.applied: If an answer is not grounded in documented evidence or a documented entry, or confidence is low, a “No documented answer” card appears instead of a guess.

standards.title: Daʿwah quality
standards.text: The audience's background, level, language and context are considered; the foundation comes before the details; and correct information is combined with clarity and good presentation, without distorting over-simplification.
standards.applied: Every answer is divided into: the Islamic principle, then custom and culture, then practical guidance — in calm language suited to a new Muslim.

standards.title: Translation and localisation
standards.text: Translation preserves the religious meaning of a term and considers the cultural context, without changing the content to meet the audience's expectations.
standards.applied: The approved glossary is built into the model; Basirah answers in the asker's language, keeping the Islamic term and explaining it; in English, the meanings of verses come from the King Fahd Complex's translation (al-Hilali & Khan).

standards.title: Transparency
standards.text: The solution discloses that it is an AI-supported tool whenever the user might think they are dealing with a human specialist.
standards.applied: A permanent notice that Basirah is an AI tool and not a mufti, and the origin of every answer is shown: the documented knowledge base, the AI, or local-references mode.

standards.title: Privacy
standards.text: Personal or sensitive data is collected only as far as needed and under a declared policy, and is not used to draw unnecessary daʿwah or religious conclusions about the user.
standards.applied: No login, and the server does not store the text of questions; bookmarks stay on your device only.

q_2_23.translation: And if you (Arab pagans, Jews, and Christians) are in doubt concerning that which We have sent down (i.e. the Qur’ân) to Our slave (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم), then produce a Sûrah (chapter) of the like thereof and call your witnesses (supporters and helpers) besides Allâh, if you are truthful.
q_2_23.arabic: وَإِن كُنتُمۡ فِي رَيۡبٖ مِّمَّا نَزَّلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا فَأۡتُواْ بِسُورَةٖ مِّن مِّثۡلِهِۦ وَٱدۡعُواْ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ

q_2_144.translation: Verily! We have seen the turning of your (Muhammad’s صلى الله عليه وسلم) face towards the heaven. Surely, We shall turn you to a Qiblah (prayer direction) that shall please you, so turn your face in the direction of Al-Masjid-al-Harâm (at Makkah). And wheresoever you people are, turn your faces (in prayer) in that direction. Certainly, the people who were given the Scripture (i.e. Jews and the Christians) know well that, that (your turning towards the direction of the Ka‘bah at Makkah in prayers) is the truth from their Lord. And Allâh is not unaware of what they do.
q_2_144.arabic: قَدۡ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجۡهِكَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبۡلَةٗ تَرۡضَىٰهَاۚ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ لَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعۡمَلُونَ

q_2_177.translation: It is not Al-Birr (piety, righteousness, and each and every act of obedience to Allâh, etc.) that you turn your faces towards east and (or) west (in prayers); but Al-Birr is (the quality of) the one who believes in Allâh, the Last Day, the Angels, the Book, the Prophets and gives his wealth, in spite of love for it, to the kinsfolk, to the orphans, and to Al-Masâkîn (the poor), and to the wayfarer, and to those who ask, and to set slaves free, performs As-Salât (Iqâmat-as-Salât ), and gives the Zakât, and who fulfil their covenant when they make it, and who are patient in extreme poverty and ailment (disease) and at the time of fighting (during the battles). Such are the people of the truth and they are Al-Muttaqûn (the pious - See V.2:2).
q_2_177.arabic: ۞ لَّيۡسَ ٱلۡبِرَّ أَن تُوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ قِبَلَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ وَلَٰكِنَّ ٱلۡبِرَّ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ وَٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَءَاتَى ٱلۡمَالَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ ذَوِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَٱلسَّآئِلِينَ وَفِي ٱلرِّقَابِ وَأَقَامَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتَى ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِهِمۡ إِذَا عَٰهَدُواْۖ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ فِي ٱلۡبَأۡسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ وَحِينَ ٱلۡبَأۡسِۗ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ صَدَقُواْۖ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُتَّقُونَ

q_2_190.translation: And fight in the Way of Allâh those who fight you, but transgress not the limits. Truly, Allâh likes not the transgressors. [This Verse is the first one that was revealed in connection with Jihâd, but it was supplemented by another (9:36)].

q_2_219.translation: They ask you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) concerning alcoholic drink and gambling. Say: "In them is a great sin, and (some) benefit for men, but the sin of them is greater than their benefit." And they ask you what they ought to spend. Say: "That which is beyond your needs." Thus Allâh makes clear to you His Laws in order that you may give thought."
q_2_219.arabic: ۞ يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡخَمۡرِ وَٱلۡمَيۡسِرِۖ قُلۡ فِيهِمَآ إِثۡمٞ كَبِيرٞ وَمَنَٰفِعُ لِلنَّاسِ وَإِثۡمُهُمَآ أَكۡبَرُ مِن نَّفۡعِهِمَاۗ وَيَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَۖ قُلِ ٱلۡعَفۡوَۗ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَفَكَّرُونَ

q_2_256.translation: There is no compulsion in religion. Verily, the Right Path has become distinct from the wrong path. Whoever disbelieves in Tâghût and believes in Allâh, then he has grasped the most trustworthy handhold that will never break. And Allâh is All-Hearer, All-Knower.
q_2_256.arabic: لَآ إِكۡرَاهَ فِي ٱلدِّينِۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشۡدُ مِنَ ٱلۡغَيِّۚ فَمَن يَكۡفُرۡ بِٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَيُؤۡمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱسۡتَمۡسَكَ بِٱلۡعُرۡوَةِ ٱلۡوُثۡقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَاۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ

q_2_286.translation: Allâh burdens not a person beyond his scope. He gets reward for that (good) which he has earned, and he is punished for that (evil) which he has earned. "Our Lord! Punish us not if we forget or fall into error, our Lord! Lay not on us a burden like that which You did lay on those before us (Jews and Christians); our Lord! Put not on us a burden greater than we have strength to bear. Pardon us and grant us Forgiveness. Have mercy on us. You are our Maulâ (Patron, Supporter and Protector, etc.) and give us victory over the disbelieving people."
q_2_286.arabic: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا ٱكۡتَسَبَتۡۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَآ إِصۡرٗا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦۖ وَٱعۡفُ عَنَّا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَآۚ أَنتَ مَوۡلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ

q_4_59.translation: O you who believe! Obey Allâh and obey the Messenger (Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم), and those of you (Muslims) who are in authority. (And) if you differ in anything amongst yourselves, refer it to Allâh and His Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم), if you believe in Allâh and in the Last Day. That is better and more suitable for final determination.
q_4_59.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِنكُمۡۖ فَإِن تَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي شَيۡءٖ فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرٞ وَأَحۡسَنُ تَأۡوِيلًا

q_4_82.translation: Do they not then consider the Qur’ân carefully? Had it been from other than Allâh, they would surely have found therein many a contradiction.

q_5_90.translation: O you who believe! Intoxicants (all kinds of alcoholic drinks), and gambling, and Al-Ansâb, and Al-Azlâm (arrows for seeking luck or decision) are an abomination of Shaitan’s (Satan) handiwork. So avoid (strictly all) that (abomination) in order that you may be successful.

q_7_26.translation: O Children of Adam! We have bestowed raiment upon you to cover yourselves (screen your private parts) and as an adornment; and the raiment of righteousness, that is better. Such are among the Ayât (proofs, evidence, verses, lessons, signs, revelations, etc.) of Allâh, that they may remember (i.e. leave falsehood and follow truth).
q_7_26.arabic: يَٰبَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ قَدۡ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمۡ لِبَاسٗا يُوَٰرِي سَوۡءَٰتِكُمۡ وَرِيشٗاۖ وَلِبَاسُ ٱلتَّقۡوَىٰ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرٞۚ ذَٰلِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ لَعَلَّهُمۡ يَذَّكَّرُونَ

q_8_38.translation: Say to those who have disbelieved, if they cease (from disbelief), their past will be forgiven. But if they return (thereto), then the examples of those (punished) before them have already preceded (as a warning).
q_8_38.arabic: قُل لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓاْ إِن يَنتَهُواْ يُغۡفَرۡ لَهُم مَّا قَدۡ سَلَفَ وَإِن يَعُودُواْ فَقَدۡ مَضَتۡ سُنَّتُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ

q_10_99.translation: And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together. So, will you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) then compel mankind, until they become believers.

q_12_108.translation: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه و سلم): "This is my way; I invite unto Allâh (i.e. to the Oneness of Allâh - Islâmic Monotheism) with sure knowledge, I and whosoever follows me (also must invite others to Allâh i.e. to the Oneness of Allâh - Islâmic Monotheism with sure knowledge). And Glorified and Exalted be Allâh (above all that they associate as partners with Him). And I am not of the Mushrikûn (polytheists, pagans, idolaters and disbelievers in the Oneness of Allâh; those who worship others along with Allâh or set up rivals or partners to Allâh)."
q_12_108.arabic: قُلۡ هَٰذِهِۦ سَبِيلِيٓ أَدۡعُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۚ عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا۠ وَمَنِ ٱتَّبَعَنِيۖ وَسُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ مِنَ ٱلۡمُشۡرِكِينَ

q_16_43.translation: And We sent not (as Our Messengers) before you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه و سلم) any but men, whom We sent revelation, (to preach and invite mankind to believe in the Oneness of Allâh). So ask (you, O pagans of Makkah) of those who know the Scripture [learned men of the Taurât (Torah) and the Injeel (Gospel)], if you know not.
q_16_43.arabic: وَمَآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا مِن قَبۡلِكَ إِلَّا رِجَالٗا نُّوحِيٓ إِلَيۡهِمۡۖ فَسۡـَٔلُوٓاْ أَهۡلَ ٱلذِّكۡرِ إِن كُنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ

q_16_125.translation: Invite (mankind, O Muhammad صلى الله عليه و سلم) to the Way of your Lord (i.e. Islâm) with wisdom (i.e. with the Divine Revelation and the Qur’ân) and fair preaching, and argue with them in a way that is better. Truly, your Lord knows best who has gone astray from His Path, and He is the Best Aware of those who are guided.
q_16_125.arabic: ٱدۡعُ إِلَىٰ سَبِيلِ رَبِّكَ بِٱلۡحِكۡمَةِ وَٱلۡمَوۡعِظَةِ ٱلۡحَسَنَةِۖ وَجَٰدِلۡهُم بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ

q_17_36.translation: And follow not (O man i.e., say not, or do not or witness not) that of which you have no knowledge. Verily! The hearing, and the sight, and the heart, of each of those one will be questioned (by Allâh).
q_17_36.arabic: وَلَا تَقۡفُ مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٌۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمۡعَ وَٱلۡبَصَرَ وَٱلۡفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنۡهُ مَسۡـُٔولٗا

q_20_14.translation: "Verily! I am Allâh! Lâ ilâha illa Ana (none has the right to be worshipped but I), so worship Me, and perform As-Salât (Iqâmat-as-Salât) for My Remembrance.

q_21_107.translation: And We have sent you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): not but as a mercy for the ‘Âlamîn (mankind, jinn and all that exists).

q_24_31.translation: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze (from looking at forbidden things), and protect their private parts (from illegal sexual acts) and not to show off their adornment except only that which is apparent (like both eyes for necessity to see the way, or outer palms of hands or one eye or dress like veil, gloves, head-cover, apron, etc.), and to draw their veils all over Juyûbihinna (i.e. their bodies, faces, necks and bosoms) and not to reveal their adornment except to their husbands, or their fathers, or their husband’s fathers, or their sons, or their husband’s sons, or their brothers or their brother’s sons, or their sister’s sons, or their (Muslim) women (i.e. their sisters in Islâm), or the (female) slaves whom their right hands possess, or old male servants who lack vigour, or small children who have no sense of feminine sex. And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment. And all of you beg Allâh to forgive you all, O believers, that you may be successful.
q_24_31.arabic: وَقُل لِّلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ يَغۡضُضۡنَ مِنۡ أَبۡصَٰرِهِنَّ وَيَحۡفَظۡنَ فُرُوجَهُنَّ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَاۖ وَلۡيَضۡرِبۡنَ بِخُمُرِهِنَّ عَلَىٰ جُيُوبِهِنَّۖ وَلَا يُبۡدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ إِلَّا لِبُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ ءَابَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ أَبۡنَآءِ بُعُولَتِهِنَّ أَوۡ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ إِخۡوَٰنِهِنَّ أَوۡ بَنِيٓ أَخَوَٰتِهِنَّ أَوۡ نِسَآئِهِنَّ أَوۡ مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُنَّ أَوِ ٱلتَّٰبِعِينَ غَيۡرِ أُوْلِي ٱلۡإِرۡبَةِ مِنَ ٱلرِّجَالِ أَوِ ٱلطِّفۡلِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَظۡهَرُواْ عَلَىٰ عَوۡرَٰتِ ٱلنِّسَآءِۖ وَلَا يَضۡرِبۡنَ بِأَرۡجُلِهِنَّ لِيُعۡلَمَ مَا يُخۡفِينَ مِن زِينَتِهِنَّۚ وَتُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ جَمِيعًا أَيُّهَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ

q_25_70.translation: Except those who repent and believe (in Islâmic Monotheism), and do righteous deeds; for those, Allâh will change their sins into good deeds, and Allâh is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
q_25_70.arabic: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلٗا صَٰلِحٗا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتٖۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورٗا رَّحِيمٗا

q_29_48.translation: Neither did you (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم) read any book before it (this Qur’ân), nor did you write any book (whatsoever) with your right hand. In that case, indeed, the followers of falsehood might have doubted.

q_30_22.translation: And among His Signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours. Verily, in that are indeed signs for men of sound knowledge.

q_31_15.translation: But if they (both) strive with you to make you join in worship with Me others that of which you have no knowledge, then obey them not; but behave with them in the world kindly, and follow the path of him who turns to Me in repentance and in obedience. Then to Me will be your return, and I shall tell you what you used to do.
q_31_15.arabic: وَإِن جَٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشۡرِكَ بِي مَا لَيۡسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلۡمٞ فَلَا تُطِعۡهُمَاۖ وَصَاحِبۡهُمَا فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا مَعۡرُوفٗاۖ وَٱتَّبِعۡ سَبِيلَ مَنۡ أَنَابَ إِلَيَّۚ ثُمَّ إِلَيَّ مَرۡجِعُكُمۡ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ

q_33_5.translation: Call them (adopted sons) by (the names of) their fathers: that is more just with Allâh. But if you know not their father’s (names, call them) your brothers in faith and Mawâlîkum (your freed slaves). And there is no sin on you concerning that in which you made a mistake, except in regard to what your hearts deliberately intend. And Allâh is Ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
q_33_5.arabic: ٱدۡعُوهُمۡ لِأٓبَآئِهِمۡ هُوَ أَقۡسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَعۡلَمُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَهُمۡ فَإِخۡوَٰنُكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَمَوَٰلِيكُمۡۚ وَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٞ فِيمَآ أَخۡطَأۡتُم بِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتۡ قُلُوبُكُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورٗا رَّحِيمًا

q_33_59.translation: O Prophet! Tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks (veils) all over their bodies (i.e. screen themselves completely except the eyes or one eye to see the way). That will be better, that they should be known (as free respectable women) so as not to be annoyed. And Allâh is Ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
q_33_59.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ وَبَنَاتِكَ وَنِسَآءِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يُدۡنِينَ عَلَيۡهِنَّ مِن جَلَٰبِيبِهِنَّۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَن يُعۡرَفۡنَ فَلَا يُؤۡذَيۡنَۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورٗا رَّحِيمٗا

q_39_53.translation: Say: "O ‘Ibâdî (My slaves) who have transgressed against themselves (by committing evil deeds and sins)! Despair not of the Mercy of Allâh: verily, Allâh forgives all sins. Truly He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
q_39_53.arabic: ۞ قُلۡ يَٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسۡرَفُواْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ لَا تَقۡنَطُواْ مِن رَّحۡمَةِ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًاۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡغَفُورُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ

q_51_56.translation: And I (Allâh) created not the jinn and mankind except that they should worship Me (Alone).

q_53_3.translation: Nor does he speak of (his own) desire. It is only a Revelation revealed.

q_60_8.translation: Allâh does not forbid you to deal justly and kindly with those who fought not against you on account of religion nor drove you out of your homes. Verily, Allâh loves those who deal with equity.

q_64_16.translation: So keep your duty to Allâh and fear Him as much as you can; listen and obey, and spend in charity; that is better for yourselves. And whosoever is saved from his own covetousness, then they are the successful ones.
q_64_16.arabic: فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ مَا ٱسۡتَطَعۡتُمۡ وَٱسۡمَعُواْ وَأَطِيعُواْ وَأَنفِقُواْ خَيۡرٗا لِّأَنفُسِكُمۡۗ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ

q_65_2.translation: Then when they are about to attain their term appointed, either take them back in a good manner or part with them in a good manner. And take as witness two just persons from among you (Muslims). And establish the testimony for Allâh. That will be an admonition given to him who believes in Allâh and the Last Day. And whosoever fears Allâh and keeps his duty to Him, He will make a way for him to get out (from every difficulty). And He will provide him from (sources) he never could imagine. And whosoever puts his trust in Allâh, then He will suffice him. Verily, Allâh will accomplish his purpose. Indeed Allâh has set a measure for all things.
q_65_2.arabic: فَإِذَا بَلَغۡنَ أَجَلَهُنَّ فَأَمۡسِكُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ فَارِقُوهُنَّ بِمَعۡرُوفٖ وَأَشۡهِدُواْ ذَوَيۡ عَدۡلٖ مِّنكُمۡ وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلشَّهَٰدَةَ لِلَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ يُوعَظُ بِهِۦ مَن كَانَ يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ وَمَن يَتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡعَل لَّهُۥ مَخۡرَجٗا ۝ وَيَرۡزُقۡهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَحۡتَسِبُۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥٓۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بَٰلِغُ أَمۡرِهِۦۚ قَدۡ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدۡرٗا

q_106_3.translation: So let them worship (Allâh) the Lord of this House (the Ka‘bah in Makkah),

q_109_6.translation: "To you be your religion, and to me my religion (Islâmic Monotheism)."

q_112.translation: Say (O Muhammad صلى الله عليه وسلم): "He is Allâh, (the) One. "Allâh-us-Samad (السيد الذي يصمد إليه في الحاجات) [Allâh the Self-Sufficient Master, Whom all creatures need, (He neither eats nor drinks)]. "He begets not, nor was He begotten. "And there is none co-equal or comparable unto Him."
